changes.now: Peter Quill, taken from Earth as a boy the night his mother died, steals an orb that Ronan the Accuser wants for Thanos. He's arrested on Xandar with Gamora, Thanos's adopted daughter, and bounty hunters Rocket and Groot, and they break out of prison with Drax, who lost his family to Ronan. The orb holds an Infinity Stone. When Ronan uses it to attack Xandar, the five hold the stone together and destroy him. Groot sacrifices himself to save them and regrows as a sapling.

changes.evidence: Groot dies shielding the group when the Dark Aster crash-lands, before the stone is used. Only four hold it: Quill grabs the stone and Gamora, Drax and Rocket share its burden to destroy Ronan.

changes.now: On TheDailyBugle.net, J. Jonah Jameson calls Spider-Man a fraud and Mysterio a hero, then airs the rest of Mysterio's video. Later, Betty Brant reports sightings of Electro and Sandman in New York, and the Bugle blames the Spider-Menace.
changes.proposed: On TheDailyBugle.net, J. Jonah Jameson calls Spider-Man a fraud and Mysterio a hero, then airs the rest of Mysterio's video. Later, Betty Brant reports strange thunderstorms and sandstorms in New York, and the Bugle blames the Spider-Menace.
changes.evidence: In the Bugle TikTok video, Betty Brant reports intense thunderstorms and sandstorms in New York and guesses supervillains may be returning, then is told to blame Spider-Man. Electro and Sandman are never named or seen. Naming them also gives away No Way Home's villains, which come next in this box's order (L2).

changes.now: Four years after the world forgot him, Peter lives alone in a small apartment and gives his whole life to being Spider-Man. The strain sets off new changes in his body, including organic webbing, and he builds an inhibitor chip to hold them back, turning to Bruce Banner, who no longer knows him. Jean Grey, a telepath whose sister died in Damage Control's experiments, takes control of the Hulk, and Peter gets through to Bruce. Frank Castle becomes an unlikely ally and hides MJ, who still doesn't know Peter. At Damage Control's Roosevelt Island facility, Peter takes off his inhibitor to fight his way past the Hand and stops Jean from killing Damage Control's director, Bill Metzger. Then he lets her into his mind, where a memory of Aunt May reaches her, and he takes the Punisher's bullet meant for her. Jean keeps him alive, and recovering, Peter sees Ned again, who says his name. After the credits, Ned's tracker shows Spider-Man somewhere in space, and no one knows why.

changes.evidence: In the final scene, Peter reintroduces himself to Ned as "Peter" and they repeat their old handshake. Ned does not say Peter's name, and the film never states that he remembers him.
